findings.title: VIEW permission is treated as MANAGE for global group operations
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-Groups resource. This no-arg check is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() via requireManage(), so an admin granted only view on all groups can create top-level groups. canManage() should require MANAGE only, as canManage(GroupModel) correctly does.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), groupResource.getId() is the internal authorization-resource UUID, while the group's ID is stored as the resource name (see AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/resolveGroup, and hasPermission() which looks resources up by name). Passing getId() to hasPermission() therefore fails the findByName lookup and falls back to the all-Groups resource, and the set returned contains authorization UUIDs rather than group IDs. Callers such as UsersResource.getUsersCount() and searchForUser() pass this set to user queries as group IDs, so counts/searches for members of a group with view-members/manage-members permission return wrong (typically empty) results.

findings.title: Existing FGAP V2 realms never get the new Groups resource or scopes
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this PR therefore never receive the new 'Groups' all-resource or the group-only scopes (manage-members, view-members, manage-membership) that init() would create from the schema. Creating a group permission in such a realm will fail when getOrCreateResource() cannot find those scopes, and getResourceTypeResource() for Groups will return null during evaluation. A migration/backfill for existing resource servers is needed.

findings.title: getResourceName does not translate group resources to group names
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases the Users resource type to return the user's username instead of the resource name (which is the user's ID), but has no equivalent branch for the new Groups resource type. Group resources are also named by their group ID, so policy/permission representations for group resources will fall through to resource.getDisplayName() and expose the group UUID rather than a human-readable group name.
